title: What are your Thoughts on Mickey Rooney?

commenti.body:
He's the annoying racist from Breakfast at Tiffany's, right?  Can't say I'm particularly fond of him.

Even putting aside the racism, which is a lot to put aside, it's one of the worst comedic performances I've ever seen in a mainstream movie, right up there with Will Ferrell in Holmes & Watson.
I was suspecting some hyperbole until I saw the Holmes and Watson and saw the righteous vitriol

I’m old and saw that film before the outrage started. Many years ago. The whole story is stupid. So she moved there and escaped a life of being in the country. What’s more infuriating is that they delete the gay aspect and turn him into her love interest. Then the guy from Beverly Hillbillies shows up. It’s a bad film and we knew back then Mickey Rooney was just one more straw in the hay bale. He doesn’t ruin the picture because it’s already bad. It’s remembered for fashion, and Moon River. Breakfast at Tiffany’s girls were like horse girls. They would do the full costume on Halloween. No one ever dressed as Mickey Rooney from that film because he’s not an important character. Back then we were just like, wow, uh ok. It’s not a good film.

* I like him. But I'm a realist. I can't deny his terrible record as a corrosive, brittle, and abusive human being. From all accounts, he was no better than the horrible Frank Fay. 

* He had a wonderful career and yes it's true Olivier considered him a stellar talent. 

* So it's better for me to say that I "like him when he's in a movie".

* I'm always chagrined to remember he was not a pleasant person in real life.

🤔

* George Peppard sure wasn't going to play an openly gay character at that date in Hollywood history. Not at that point in his career. No leading male would have. 

* Can we blame the studios for this? Not hardly. LGBT stories just weren't done circulated at that point in time. Hollywood is inherently conservative; the USA is inherently conservative.

* Rooney's character was obviously a painfully inept spoof. He wears a kimono, horn-rimmed spectacles, and false teeth --buck teeth --in his mouth. He speaks pidgin Japanese. His 'hobby' is 'intimate photography'. Everything about it was horrendous. It doesn't even need to be harped on. But Rooney was a veteran Hollywood actor despite this ridiculous and embarrassing role. The whole assignment was offensive.

* But the resulting film is nonetheless a Hollywood classic romance. It stems from the wonderfully-written novella by Truman Capote. Capote was one of America's finest authors and the movie does capture some small shred of what he wrote. 

* What else should an this famous Audrey Hepburn film have been, exactly? What should it have been otherwise than what it was? Would it have been guaranteed to have been better as another "Children's Hour"? Not necessarily at all.

* Capote's little story wasn't F Scott Fitzgerald or Henry James. It just a sweet, sentimental little novella. So these 20/20 hindsight agendas aren't fair to anyone. 

* If there was any factor which could certainly have killed the movie it was Truman Capote himself. Flamingly flamboyant in a manner as silly as Rip Taylor; alcoholic; overweight; petty; drug addict. Filming a movie faithful to whatever he might have wished would never have worked no matter what.  

* Hollywood isn't located in Greenwich Village at the time, and didn't exist to cater to New Yorkers. Gvill has Broadway and off-Broadway for its various fetishes. California was in the business of making movies to serve the entire USA.

* Today things are different. But that's thanks to the new word of viral marketing. Modern Hollywood can't do otherwise but serve special-interests in today's day and age. So in the end, everyone wins. 

Just sayin...
* In sum: it's to no good purpose to go around back-biting a classic romance.

Friend of mine had a weird encounter sometime in the 90s -- he was in an empty bar getting ready to soundcheck with his band, and an old guy wandered in, talking to no one in particular a million miles per minute, mostly racist stuff. My friend was like, "dude, please chill out a bit," and the reply was "do you know who I am? do you know who I am? I'm Mickey Rooney -- fuck you, asshole!"
Yeah, I’m familiar with the history of Hollywood. And the era this film was made in. I get why they changed it.
